subproblems.title: Compact exhaustion of an open subset of ℝ^P
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)) be open. Then there is a sequence (K_i)_{i∈ℕ} of compact subsets of ℝ^P such that K_i ⊆ U for every i ∈ ℕ, and every compact set C ⊆ ℝ^P with C ⊆ U is contained in K_i for some i ∈ ℕ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → ∃ K : ℕ → Set (Euclid P), (∀ i, IsCompact (K i)) ∧ (∀ i, K i ⊆ U) ∧ ∀ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → ∃ i, C ⊆ K i
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (exhaustion of U), re-indexed from i = 0 (K_i below plays the role of the parent's K_{i+1}, with radius i+1 and margin 1/(i+1)). The parent's last bullet ("every compact C ⊆ U lies in some K_i") is proved here directly from a uniform positive distance between C and ℝ^P ∖ U, instead of through interiors and a finite subcover; this needs fewer auxiliary facts. The defining condition is a pointwise inequality over all y ∉ U, so no case split for U = ∅ or U = ℝ^P is needed. Mathlib's convention infDist x ∅ = 0 would otherwise break the case U = ℝ^P.

Let P ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open.

1. Definition. For i ∈ ℕ put r_i := 1/(i+1) > 0 and
   K_i := B̄(0, i+1) ∩ ⋂_{y ∈ ℝ^P ∖ U} {x ∈ ℝ^P : r_i ≤ dist(x, y)},
   where B̄(0, i+1) := {x : ‖x‖ ≤ i+1}. In Lean: K := fun i => closedBall (0 : Euclid P) ((i : ℝ) + 1) ∩ ⋂ y ∈ Uᶜ, {x | 1 / ((i : ℝ) + 1) ≤ dist x y}. When U = ℝ^P the intersection over y has an empty index set, so K_i = B̄(0, i+1).

2. Each K_i is compact.
 - For fixed y, the set {x : r_i ≤ dist(x, y)} is closed, because x ↦ dist(x, y) is continuous. In Lean: isClosed_le continuous_const (continuous_id.dist continuous_const).
 - An arbitrary intersection of closed sets is closed (isClosed_biInter).
 - The closed ball B̄(0, i+1) of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P is compact (Heine–Borel; isCompact_closedBall).
 - A compact set intersected with a closed set is compact (IsCompact.inter_right). Hence K_i is compact.

3. Each K_i ⊆ U. Let x ∈ K_i and suppose x ∉ U. Then y := x is an index of the intersection, so r_i ≤ dist(x, x) = 0. This contradicts r_i = 1/(i+1) > 0. Hence x ∈ U.

4. A uniform margin around a compact subset. Let C ⊆ ℝ^P be compact with C ⊆ U.
 - Since C is compact, U is open and C ⊆ U, there is δ > 0 such that the open δ-thickening thickening(δ, C) := {y : ∃ z ∈ C, dist(y, z) < δ} is contained in U. In Mathlib: IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open hC hU hCU.
 - Elementary justification. If C = ∅, take δ := 1. Otherwise, for each z ∈ C choose ρ_z > 0 with B(z, 2ρ_z) ⊆ U, which is possible because U is open. Finitely many balls B(z_1, ρ_1), …, B(z_m, ρ_m) cover C; put δ := min_j ρ_j > 0. If dist(y, z) < δ with z ∈ C, pick j with dist(z, z_j) < ρ_j. Then dist(y, z_j) < δ + ρ_j ≤ 2ρ_j, so y ∈ U.
 - Consequence: for every x ∈ C and every y ∈ ℝ^P ∖ U, δ ≤ dist(x, y). Indeed y ∉ U gives y ∉ thickening(δ, C), i.e. dist(y, z) ≥ δ for all z ∈ C (mem_thickening_iff). Take z = x and use symmetry of dist.

5. Boundedness. C is compact, hence bounded, so there is R ∈ ℝ with ‖x‖ ≤ R for all x ∈ C (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall).

6. Choice of the index. By the Archimedean property, choose N ∈ ℕ with 1/(N+1) < δ (exists_nat_one_div_lt) and M ∈ ℕ with R ≤ M (exists_nat_ge). Let i := max(N, M).
 - Since M ≤ i, R ≤ M ≤ i + 1.
 - Since N ≤ i, r_i = 1/(i+1) ≤ 1/(N+1) < δ.

7. C ⊆ K_i. Let x ∈ C.
 - By steps 5 and 6, ‖x‖ ≤ R ≤ i + 1, so x ∈ B̄(0, i+1).
 - For each y ∈ ℝ^P ∖ U, steps 4 and 6 give r_i < δ ≤ dist(x, y).
 - So x lies in every set of the intersection, and x ∈ K_i.

8. Conclusion. The sets K_i of step 1 are compact (step 2) and contained in U (step 3), and every compact C ⊆ U lies in some K_i (steps 4–7). ∎
proof_key_steps: Define K_i := closedBall 0 (i+1) ∩ ⋂_{y ∉ U} {x : 1/(i+1) ≤ dist x y}; no case split on U is needed.
K_i is compact (closed ball ∩ intersection of closed sets) and K_i ⊆ U (x ∉ U would give 1/(i+1) ≤ dist x x = 0).
For compact C ⊆ U pick δ > 0 with thickening δ C ⊆ U (so dist(x, y) ≥ δ for x ∈ C, y ∉ U) and R with C ⊆ closedBall 0 R.
With i := max(N, M), where 1/(N+1) < δ and R ≤ M, every x ∈ C satisfies the defining conditions of K_i, so C ⊆ K_i.

subproblems.title: The space of n-covectors on ℝ^P is finite-dimensional
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, the real vector space Covector (Euclid P) n = Λⁿ(ℝ^P) of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication, is finite-dimensional over ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the fact "Λⁿ, Λ^{n+1} are finite-dimensional", used without proof in step 3 of the parent proof. Mathlib has no FiniteDimensional, ProperSpace or SecondCountableTopology instance for Covector (Euclid P) n = (Euclid P) [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ, and instance synthesis fails, so the fact must be proved. The frozen type and the argument below are those of the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dor_ims_lusin_covector_finiteDimensional. Three other accepted declarations have the identical type: dor_ims_sua_covector_finiteDimensional, imsupp_covector_finiteDimensional and lcn_covector_finiteDimensional. None of them is in this branch's proof base 7d35af49, so the fact is supplied as a sibling.

Let P, n ∈ ℕ.

1. Let e = (e_0, …, e_{P−1}) be the standard basis of ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). In Lean: e := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis.

2. Define L : Covector (Euclid P) n → ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ) by L(α)(I) := α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), i.e. L α I = α (fun k => e (I k)).
 - L is ℝ-linear, because covectors are added and scaled pointwise: (α + β)(v) = α(v) + β(v) and (c • α)(v) = c · α(v) for every n-tuple v.
 - So L(α + β) = L α + L β and L(c • α) = c • L α; both hold definitionally (rfl).

3. L is injective. Suppose L α = L β.
 - Then α and β agree on every n-tuple (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) of basis vectors.
 - An alternating multilinear map is determined by its values on tuples of basis vectors. Expanding each argument in the basis e and using multilinearity writes α(v_0, …, v_{n−1}) as a finite linear combination of the values α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}). In Lean: Module.Basis.ext_alternating e, applied to fun v _ => congrFun h v.
 - Hence α and β have the same underlying alternating map. A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective), so α = β.

4. Conclusion. The space (Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ of real functions on a finite set is finite-dimensional. A vector space with an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective L hL). Hence Covector (Euclid P) n is finite-dimensional over ℝ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the standard basis e of ℝ^P.
Define the linear map L α := (α(e ∘ I))_{I : Fin n → Fin P} into the finite-dimensional space (Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ.
L is injective: an alternating map is determined by its values on basis tuples (Basis.ext_alternating), and toAlternatingMap is injective.

subproblems.title: Test forms supported in a fixed compact set have a countable subfamily approximating ω and dω uniformly
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. Then there is a countable set D ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n: C^∞ compactly supported n-forms on ℝ^P with tsupport in U) such that tsupport η ⊆ K for every η ∈ D, with the following property. For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K and every real ε > 0 there is η ∈ D such that, for every x ∈ ℝ^P, dist(ω(x), η(x)) < ε and dist(dω(x), dη(x)) < ε. Here d = exteriorDerivative, and dist(a, b) = ‖a − b‖ is the operator-norm distance on Covector (Euclid P) n, respectively Covector (Euclid P) (n+1).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → ∃ D : Set (TestFormOn U n), D.Countable ∧ (∀ η ∈ D, tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ η ∈ D, (∀ x, dist ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) < ε) ∧ ∀ x, dist (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) (exteriorDerivative (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) < ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the parent proof (the pieces X_i, the embedding ω ↦ (ω|_{K_i}, dω|_{K_i}) into a separable space of continuous maps on K_i, and the pulled-back countable dense subset), specialized to one compact set K. Two details are filled in:
 - (a) Mathlib cannot infer finite-dimensionality or second countability of Covector (Euclid P) k, so it is taken from the sibling covector_findim.
 - (b) Instead of the full isometry claim for the sum metric d_i, only two facts are used: pointwise distance ≤ uniform distance on K, and vanishing off K. This is exactly what step 6 of the parent proof needs.
Neither K ⊆ U nor openness of U is used.

Notation: Λ^k := Covector (Euclid P) k with its operator norm, so dist(a, b) = ‖a − b‖. d = exteriorDerivative. X := {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ K}.

1. Regularity and vanishing. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n).
 - By definition ω is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U. In particular ω is continuous (Lean: ω.property.1.1.continuous).
 - dω is again a test form (SimonGMT Chapter06 exteriorDerivative_isTestForm ω.property.1), hence continuous.
 - If x ∉ tsupport ω then ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
 - tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so also dω(x) = 0.
 - Consequently, for ω ∈ X and x ∉ K: x ∉ tsupport ω, hence ω(x) = 0 and dω(x) = 0.

2. The target space.
 - By the sibling theorem covector_findim (with n and with n + 1), Λⁿ and Λ^{n+1} are finite-dimensional real normed spaces.
 - A finite-dimensional real normed space is proper (FiniteDimensional.proper), and a proper metric space is second countable (secondCountable_of_proper).
 - Let F := Λⁿ × Λ^{n+1} with the product metric dist((a, b), (a', b')) = max(dist(a, a'), dist(b, b')) (Prod.dist_eq). As a product of two second-countable spaces, F is second countable.

3. The function space. Give K the subspace topology.
 - K is compact (isCompact_iff_compactSpace) and Hausdorff, hence locally compact. It is second countable as a subspace of ℝ^P.
 - Therefore C(K, F), the continuous maps K → F with the compact-open topology, is second countable. This is ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology in Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/SecondCountableSpace.lean; that module must be imported in Submission.lean.
 - Since K is compact, C(K, F) carries the uniform metric dist(f, g) = sup_{x ∈ K} dist(f(x), g(x)). Its topology is the compact-open topology: Mathlib's metric instance on C(K, F) is pulled back along the uniform embedding into bounded continuous functions.
 - For every x ∈ K, dist(f(x), g(x)) ≤ dist(f, g) (ContinuousMap.dist_apply_le_dist).

4. The map Φ. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), let Φ(ω) ∈ C(K, F) be the map K ∋ x ↦ (ω(x), dω(x)). It is continuous: x ↦ (ω(x), dω(x)) is continuous on ℝ^P by step 1 (Continuous.prodMk), and the inclusion K → ℝ^P is continuous.

5. A countable dense subset of Φ(X) and its pull-back.
 - The image Φ(X) is a subspace of the second-countable space C(K, F), hence second countable and separable. So there is a countable set T ⊆ Φ(X) that is dense in Φ(X) (TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense applied to the subtype Φ '' X).
 - Every t ∈ Φ(X) has the form Φ(ω) with ω ∈ X. By choice fix σ(t) ∈ X with Φ(σ(t)) = t.
 - Define D := σ(T) = {σ(t) : t ∈ T} ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(U).

6. Properties of D. D is countable, as the image of the countable set T. Every η ∈ D equals σ(t) ∈ X for some t, so tsupport η ⊆ K.

7. Approximation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K, i.e. ω ∈ X, and let ε > 0.
 - Φ(ω) ∈ Φ(X), and T is dense in the metric space Φ(X) with the restricted distance. So there is t ∈ T with dist(Φ(ω), t) < ε (Dense.exists_dist_lt).
 - Put η := σ(t) ∈ D. Then Φ(η) = t, so dist(Φ(ω), Φ(η)) < ε. Let x ∈ ℝ^P.
 - (a) If x ∈ K, steps 2 and 3 give max(dist(ω(x), η(x)), dist(dω(x), dη(x))) = dist(Φ(ω)(x), Φ(η)(x)) ≤ dist(Φ(ω), Φ(η)) < ε. So dist(ω(x), η(x)) < ε and dist(dω(x), dη(x)) < ε.
 - (b) If x ∉ K, then ω ∈ X and η ∈ X, so step 1 gives ω(x) = 0 = η(x) and dω(x) = 0 = dη(x). Both distances are 0 < ε.
 - Hence dist(ω(x), η(x)) < ε and dist(dω(x), dη(x)) < ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.

8. Conclusion. D is countable and all its members are supported in K (step 6). Step 7 gives the required approximation for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K and every ε > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Test forms and their exterior derivatives are continuous and vanish off tsupport ω; for ω supported in K, both vanish off K.
By the sibling covector_findim, F := Λⁿ × Λ^{n+1} is finite-dimensional, hence proper and second countable.
For compact K, C(K, F) is second countable and carries the sup metric, with dist(f x, g x) ≤ dist f g.
Map X = {ω : tsupport ω ⊆ K} by Φ(ω) := (ω, dω)|_K; take a countable dense T ⊆ Φ(X) and pull it back by choice to D ⊆ X.
For ω ∈ X and ε > 0, pick η ∈ D with dist(Φω, Φη) < ε. This bounds both pointwise distances on K; off K all values are 0.
